title: ack_always uses different API pattern than ack_on_error
description:
The two reliable fragmentation modes have inconsistent APIs:

ack_on_error:
- `AckOnErrorSender::new(payload: &'a [u8], rule_id, dtag, receiver_limit)`
- Takes a reference to external payload
- Caller owns the buffer

ack_always:
- `Sender::new(rule_id, dtag, max_retries)` + `sender.start(packet: &[u8])`
- Copies packet into internal 1280-byte buffer
- Two-phase initialization (new + start)

What goes wrong: Users switching between modes must learn different patterns. The ack_always approach wastes memory (see separate issue) and requires an extra method call.

Suggested alignment with ack_on_error pattern:
```rust
// ack_always::Sender
pub fn new(
    payload: &'a [u8],
    rule_id: u8,
    dtag: u8,
    max_retries: u8,
) -> Result<Self, FragmentError>
```

This also fixes the memory issue by taking a reference.

close_reason: Aligned ack_always API with ack_on_error: Sender::new takes receiver_limit, start() returns Result, added get_fragment()/iter()/handle_ack(), Receiver::new takes only storage (infers rule_id/dtag from first fragment), receive() takes Fragment and returns ReceiverResult with response/packet_len/rcs_ok/aborted fields
